We’re thrilled to announce the launch of our Delegators Reward Program, an opportunity for you to support the WorldMapPin project while earning rewards simultaneously. This is another big step in the evolution of this great project that we all love. ### How It All Started The idea popped out during a delightful breakfast at Hivefest when @roelandp asked @detlev and @lizanomadsoul if we had a plan about rewarding our delegators. Since then, we've put a lot of thought into creating a program that not only rewards you, our amazing supporters but also strengthens the Hive ecosystem. Big thank you to @arcange for coding and testing the system for the project. ### Why a Delegators Reward Program? The program aims at rewarding anyone who delegates at least 50 HP to @worldmappin in order to give back as a thank-you for their delegation. By delegating Hive Power to @worldmappin, you become an integral part of our project, supporting the curation of daily travel content and receiving a share of the curation rewards proportional to your delegation. The @worldmappin team curates travel content daily and votes for the best English and Spanish posts. Our curation rewards are quite high as we are very active in curating quality content. Our average curation APR ranges from 9% to 11%, which our delegators will also benefit from. ### How does it work? Several other projects on HIVE reward their delegators with HIVE, HBD, or with their own tokens. At @worldmappin, we have decided to reward our delegators with Hive Power (HP). The main reasons to do so are: - We will grow together - If you were doing your own curation, you would also receive Hive Power - It is a healthy way to support the Hive Eco System. We will share 80% of our curation rewards with our delegator. The remaining will be used to grow the @worldmappin account and provide greater rewards to the talented authors we curate. *Note: for efficiency reasons, we will not distribute a reward if its amount is less than 0.005 HP. With a delegation of at least 50 HP, this should not be an issue.* ### When? Our Delegators Reward Program will start on **November 1st**! This means we will collect data on curation rewards and delegations once the day is over. Only after that our delegators will receive their rewards. [Léelo en **español** aquí](#spanish)
![Authorized picture by @lizanomadsoul](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/EphwvnseGpoFsqerip5DYGfvbjMnpcP2dKvEaiP5Ezhaad1uqpdt9YswSrDWH917stk.jpg) # Our goal at Worldmappin Map and Travel Community Since **the worldmappin.com map** exists we have planned to extend it for all Hive users, which means everyone can pin their post on the map and link it to the content-related community - bringing all the users and communities together in one place again the worldmappin.com map. **The Worldmappin Community** is the start of showing how that works. It always has been and will be travel-related, because our vision in this **community** has always been two things: A: Provide each traveler with their unique world map, where they can explore the world, pin their trips and memories, and dive back into the memories whenever they want with just a click. B: Give the travelers a platform to share their adventures and experiences with others, so that the whole community benefits from using the map as a travel guide to finding more information and inspiration for their next trips. As you know the curation team of @worldmappin project: @lizanomadsoul, @ybanezkim26, @lauramica, @glecerioberto, and @ninaeatshere, is checking the incoming travel posts of this community every day, curating the top content and giving the winners visibility in our Daily Travel Digest. We often get questions from our community members on what to do and not do, or how they can improve their content to get curated by our team. So we took some time within the team to write down our guidelines with all the rules and suggestions, on which you can rely when writing a travel post within the @Worldmappin community. In this post, we will go into detail about every one of them. - Thanks also to @livinguktaiwan and the rest of the @worldmappin team @detlev, @arcange, @godfish,@louis88, @rivalzzz, @masterswatch and @uniforced for your input and for the support on this. ![Bildschirmfoto 2024-10-10 um 19.17.17.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23w3EVhVkZqLVzF3s3wB8HBA6aoHDSZnwZ4rjrPDKzQj9Gi5wqtBKyYnjq4EQXm7J79wT.png) For us, it is important, that all of you have the same knowledge and possibilities to position your content within this community following the standards of quality that we seek to ensure following our vision. ![Authorized picture by @bil.prag](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23tvkkLbUnByuUE82pY5LHSVDy7hfUmnA9fEPDvhmPzSGJBpQPekoqp9yUjqtax4CrvFY.jpeg) # Intro We love and celebrate the huge diversity in our community, representing different cultures, customs, mentalities, genders, age groups, and languages. Every traveler has his/her unique character, perception of the world, values, and strengths that make him/her the special person that we love to follow on their trips. We are very aware that with this uniqueness there comes different styles of writing, taking pictures or telling a story and that is super great! So of course, this summary is meant only as a suggestion! We love and understand that HIVE is a decentralized ecosystem, where we are all free to create content in our own individual way! However, if you share our goal and want to get support for your efforts, you may want to consider certain rules and suggestions for your future posts, that allow us to establish a standard of quality. # So let's get started! Read further and get more clear on these things on the way! ![Authorized picture by @lizanomadsoul](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23xoueMQMECcMBErfM1aCGiDLJkg2Y2xcvtwnRnCg7WA5SBVSsTeKdAvV1teUt7yv6q75.jpg) ## Rules for posting in the community As you may know, every community has its own rules. The rules are our most important guidelines to follow our vision and keep the quality for every one of you. If you want to be in this community you have to follow them, otherwise you will be muted at some point. Those rules have been implemented since the beginning of the project and are regularly updated. ### Rule Nr. 1. This community is only for posts included in the https://worldmappin.com map. The most important rule of our community is to pin your post to our map, because for us it's not only important that you can collect your posts on your map, but also that other travelers can benefit from your experiences. Of course, this will also give your post more exposure, as well as a chance to be featured in our daily Travel Digest 😃. There are two ways to pin your post to the map: - Include PINs from PeakD: After writing your post, click on the map icon at the bottom. It's next to “ Short preview description” and above the “Advanced” icon. ![Bildschirmfoto 2024-10-10 um 20.00.51.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/Eo6SchkLfuZGRfoyFcwgv3N2WiVnFNP38U8cifkis662bFNF1j2PzpwdcYQDjD7Amhq.png) - Include PINs in the rest of the Front-ends: - Go to https://worldmappin.com/ - Find the location of your publication on the map, you can do this by scrolling the map or using the search bar. - Click on the GET CODE button and then click on the exact location of your publication: a code snippet will be generated. - Copy the code and paste it into the draft of your Hive post. Then publish it. 🙂 - The code will be invisible in your post, but a few minutes after publishing you will receive a comment informing you that your post has been added to the map. ![Bildschirmfoto 2024-10-10 um 20.01.24.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23wgUJT7kkrRyKQsXSLrRbivrgJ18h3sPeyGJVnZFTJDV8H1Xco8EN1zcJdXtpDQrCQUo.png) ### Rule Nr. 2. English and Spanish content only. (or bi-lingual with one of the languages being English or Spanish) As we want this map to be understandable for most of our users and we are still growing. We only allow English or Spanish content for now. Of course we plan to extend this rule to more languages over time but for now only those two languages are allowed and being curated. If your native language is not English, feel free to include the original version of your writing in your native language next to the English or Spanish text. ### Rule Nr. 3. Only original content, no plagiarism, no AI-generated content, no recycled content. We want to know what you experienced! See your Pictures and get shared your personal knowledge - so we can be on the trip together and follow your adventures just the way you did! So please only use information, pictures, or videos that are yours (or put the source). Plagiarism is not allowed because of obvious reasons. We know that AI is the future, it is fun and that of course it can help put more value on your post sometimes, but there are also some users out there, who are writing their posts using AI only - trying to use it only to get some payout - not to share their trip experiences with others. So for us, a mix is ok, but we will know if it is 100% AI generated and that is fully against our rules as it is also not you - and therefore not following our vision and values. Recycling old posts and pictures same as writing multiple times about the same place /the same experience is not allowed for the same reasons. ### Rule Nr. 4. Content must be about places you have personally traveled to and about your experience. We want you to explore your own map, make your own experiences and share them with the community, so they get inspired to do something like that as well! We love to be on your side when you are getting out of your comfort zone, taking on new adventures and checking out new places. So don´t just plan it theoretically - go, do it, and write about it after you experience it yourself! ### Rule Nr. 5. Worldmappin is a travel community, please post reviews of accommodations, food, and restaurants in other appropriate communities. Please avoid posting on unrelated topics. This also includes - reviews about accommodations - shopping malls - restaurants - tips & tricks on transportation unless they are only a small part of your trip and not the main topic of the post OR such a place of interest to travel to, because of historic /extra cool background. However, you can pin your posts from other communities on the map, to keep track of all your visits on https://worldmappin.com. Here are some examples (click on each image to see details): |[Actifit community](https://peakd.com/c/hive-193552/created) |[BEER community](https://peakd.com/c/hive-187719/created) |[HiveFest community](https://peakd.com/c/hive-106258/created)| |-|-|-| |
[![](https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://usermedia.actifit.io/D9DCB68D-D042-45C3-80E3-739DF4AE1581638640735517426688)](https://peakd.com/hive-193552/@ninaeatshere/actifit-ninaeatshere-20241009t182346898z)
|
[![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbpc9YajQkcxGv9kMtTkGGXMLfq3B4WSTKiriGbKDXBXz/img_3344.jpg)](https://peakd.com/hive-187719/@ninaeatshere/beer-tasting-at-hivefest-split)
| [![](https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EoGyotE2GeJxou8KqraF6yzEnaPDAYshQ2Q4njiwdHRzCKxJCNQdauwGysDMKm9XWzx.jpeg)](https://peakd.com/hive-106258/@ninaeatshere/restaurant-gusar-hivefest-gala-dinner-or-engesp) | | [![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/Eo2BSgYeWqHyJeFCtZdKFTZdQcDyUJUersW5YPavQEspAyECJkZbG9sjAc6m2noLD6i.png)](https://peakd.com/hive-193552/@worldmappin/wmp1728499187646)| [![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23tHbkj8CLsRWaYya87AmM3xbgqg1UYTcLfvycps5qRkU18MhVUwRfMvGWquhuWrVmesi.png)](https://peakd.com/hive-187719/@worldmappin/wmp1727017768292)| [![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23tHbg1MP4BtYk2Qt8dEtzJ46Ld83kwSwpzMEZVNeGrJD9ojyvgMQpVyPsqFFjQJ9HmH6.png)](https://peakd.com/hive-106258/@worldmappin/wmp1726526214980)| ### Rule Nr. 6. Penalties that happen if you don´t follow the rules If you don´t follow our community rules, you will be muted. Depending on which rule you are breaking, you get a warning and will be watched or muted right away. As the general consensus within Hive is that plagiarized content, AI-generated, spam, and recycled posts meant to farm rewards are to be muted, and users involved in those activities are to be penalized by blacklisting from further curation, here we are very strict and act right away. If you break one of the other rules you will get a friendly reminder and will be put on our watchlist. If it happens again you will be muted again. - If you are having trouble with this or you have questions on it you can get in touch with us on [Discord Channel](https://discord.gg/EGtBvSM) at any time. ![Authorized picture by @lizanomadsoul](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/EqBbJbYvcJYiErfDBaRHrRiwc7M95b4LRZV3u1CUZwZRuQR1MDpFsiiZEcvbCSTrTqv.jpeg) ## Suggestions Congrats! You have made it through the rule jungle and are enjoying the view as all the fog should be gone by now. As a big thank you for your attention and because you are a great member of this community, we want to give you a small collection of suggestions to make your content even more exciting for others to read. Of course, those things can also help to be selected by us in the daily Traveldigest. ### Headline of the post On Hive, hundreds of posts are published every day, so it is very difficult for curators to cover all the content. The title we choose is the first piece of information we see from your work, so it is important that the title of your post is short, attractive, and related to the content you submit. There is no single way, but in terms of travel content, it is advisable to indicate the location or the name of the place you visit instead or in addition to your invitation to read the content of an adventure. It is recommended to avoid long titles, there is just no need to detail itineraries or exalt the headline, so get to the point 😎. ### Bilingual posts As we told you already in the rules section: If your native language is not English, feel free to include the original version of your writing in your native language. This helps us to verify the authenticity of the text and allows you to have a wider audience and interactions with people who also speak the same language as you. Of course, always include the English translation. When you do so, please make it visually attractive and easy to follow. As for the way to distribute the content in different languages, there are many possibilities (one language first followed by the other, translation by blocks of content or in different columns, among others) and all of them are valid, the important thing is that the way you present it allows the reader to feel comfortable when reading your content. Try to put yourself on the reader's side. As for the **title**, try to point out the languages in which it is available, no need to be redundant. Here are some examples, there can be many variations of this, but the best is to indicate only once in the sentence the presence of each language: *e.g.1 “My post headline [Eng][Esp]” e.g.2 “El título de mi post [Esp][Eng]” e.g.3 “My post headline | El título de mi post”*. ### Length of content Travel and adventure are words that by themselves open our imagination to countless stories. Remember that our goal in this community is to invite others to accompany us during the travels and serve as a guide to visit. You write about your experiences and let others know about the spots you have enjoyed the most. It is difficult to summarize them in just 300 words. Of course you can, but is it enough to make your experience the best of the day? By this, we don't mean that we write a lot just to increase volume, nor that your publications have to be full of historical/technical data obtained from other sources. What we love is for you to take us on a journey with you, with your emotions and sensations through the journey that many can make, but that has been unique for you. The moment you to tell us your own story, what particularly inspired you to talk about it, it is not difficult to reach **at least 500 words**, which could be considered as a starting point to stand out. ![Authorized gif by @ninaeatshere](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23xVMRr2moLd8z8im7sHAq2k8EfG9PfHVPrcL9fZG5vGYtn18KNTspFHUgTZai8xPZed6.gif) ### Photos and videos This is another important feature that immediately captures the reader's attention. Choosing and highlighting your images can be crucial when promoting your publication, but you must not forget that the essence of a travel post is your story, the experience, and the anecdotes that allow you to capture those moments with which you illustrate your blog. We recommend finding a balance between photos and text. You can use as many photos as you want, but remember that these serve as backup to your story, this community is not about photography, so publishing 20 photos and 100 words, is not as interesting as a travel guide. On the other side sharing only 3 images that do not highlight that incredible journey is also not telling so much about your adventure. Therefore, a basic recommendation would be to include at least 5 photos of the environment we visited, showing the landscape, the town, or the monuments. Taking pictures of ourselves during the tour, selfies, and photos of food and lodging is super nice to see, but cannot be the main part of the audiovisual material, remember that the community is focused on the traveler's destination. Try to take care of the quality of the photographs. Lack of focus and leaning without seeking dynamism or any other form of artistic expression, end up in images that are difficult to understand. As for **the videos, regardless of the length, there is no justifying the lack of text and images** sharing our experience. Not everyone has the time to watch a whole video, the best thing is to offer the viewer both options so that we not only have video views but also invite readers to enjoy our experience. We recommend orienting the device used for recording horizontally so that it is more friendly to the eye in 3Speak. ### Sources, quotations, rights, and credits We have emphasized the importance of sharing original content, based on personal experience and according to rules 3 and 4 of the community, so it might go without saying that the text, images, and other resources used in the publication must be our own. However, for specific occasions within the post, when we share an image or video **authorized** by third parties, we must give credit to the authors and link to the source link to verify its veracity. This is not a problem if we do not base our entire article on someone else's reference, but we introduce an element to improve the story we have been sharing with others. ### Tags In any case, in Hive tags must be related to the content you are writing about. Within the community, we don't require any in particular, but #Travel will help you classify your content, making it more accessible when someone is interested in this topic. Some relevant monuments or features of the place visited are #beach, #nature, #forest, #mountain, #lake. If you include a language other than English, use the tag of your language of origin and some reference to travel (e.g. #Spanish, #viajes, #senderismo #deutsch). ![Authorized picture by @louis88](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EpvhuUYiyc9pAWJeemu1ss6qhkNptprFMgLr5LDuNr4KGWC9YLjkQxZGjS57ReLovws.jpeg) # Engagement Last but not least, as important as all the previous sections, the commitment of each user within the blockchain and especially in the community is fundamental. Has conseguido atravesar la jungla de reglas y estás disfrutando de la vista, ya que toda la niebla debería haberse disipado ya. Como gran agradecimiento por tu atención y porque eres un gran miembro de esta comunidad, queremos darte una pequeña colección de sugerencias para que tu contenido sea aún más emocionante de leer para los demás. Por supuesto, esas cosas también pueden ayudar a ser seleccionado por nosotros en el Traveldigest diario. ### Título del post En Hive se publican cientos de posts cada día, por lo que es muy difícil para los curadores abarcar todo el contenido. El título que elegimos es la primera información que vemos de tu trabajo, por lo que es importante que el título de tu publicación sea corto, atractivo y esté relacionado con el contenido que presentas. No hay una forma única, pero en términos de contenido de viaje, es aconsejable indicar la ubicación o el nombre del lugar que visitas en vez, o además, de tu invitación a leer el contenido de una aventura. Se recomienda evitar los títulos largos, no hace falta detallar itinerarios ni exaltar el título, así que ve al grano 😎. ### Publicaciones bilingües Como ya te dijimos en la sección de normas: Si tu lengua materna no es el inglés, no dudes en incluir la versión original de tu escrito en tu lengua de origen. Esto nos ayuda a verificar la autenticidad del texto y te permite tener una audiencia más amplia e interactuar con personas que también hablan el mismo idioma que tú. Por supuesto, incluye siempre la traducción al inglés. Cuando lo hagas, procura que sea visualmente atractivo y fácil de seguir. En cuanto a la forma de distribuir el contenido en diferentes idiomas, hay muchas posibilidades (un idioma primero seguido del otro, traducción por bloques de contenido o en diferentes columnas, entre otras) y todas son válidas, lo importante es que la forma en que lo presentes permita al lector sentirse cómodo al momento de leer tu contenido. Intenta ponerte en el lugar del lector. En cuanto al **título**, intenta señalar los idiomas en los que está disponible, no hace falta ser redundante. He aquí algunos ejemplos, puede haber muchas variantes, pero lo mejor es indicar una sola vez en la frase la presencia de cada idioma: *e. j.1 "El título de mi post [Esp][Eng]" e. j. 2 "My post headline [Eng][Esp]" e. j. 3 "El título de mi post | My post headline"*. ### Extensión del contenido Viaje y aventura son palabras que por sí solas despiertan nuestra imaginación a innumerables historias. Recuerda que nuestro objetivo en esta comunidad es invitar a otros a acompañarnos durante los viajes y servir de guía para su visita. Escribe sobre tus experiencias y da a conocer a los demás los lugares que más te han gustado. Es difícil resumirlos en sólo 300 palabras. Claro que puedes, pero ¿es suficiente para que tu experiencia sea la mejor de todas a lo largo del día? Con esto no queremos decir que escribas mucho sólo para incrementar el volumen, ni que tus publicaciones tengan que estar llenas de datos históricos/técnicos obtenidos de otras fuentes. Lo que nos encanta es que nos lleves de viaje contigo, con tus emociones y sensaciones a través del recorrido que muchos pueden hacer, pero que para ti ha sido único. En el momento en que nos cuentes tu propia historia, lo que te ha inspirado especialmente para hablar de ello, no es difícil llegar a **al menos 500 palabras**, lo que podría considerarse como un punto de partida para sobresalir. ![Gif autorizado por @ninaeatshere](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/241tQTPAaoSvjN9G5z3mBNQS3XaSMPsPBceZbR5WwdZXYC9pHGsm2VAdJwwrLX1icFiib.gif) ### Fotos y vídeos Este es otro elemento importante que capta inmediatamente la atención del lector. Elegir y destacar tus imágenes puede ser crucial a la hora de promocionar tu publicación, pero no debes olvidar que la esencia de un post de viajes es tu historia, la experiencia y las anécdotas que te permiten capturar esos momentos con los que ilustras tu blog. Te recomendamos que encuentres un equilibrio entre fotos y texto. Puedes utilizar todas las fotos que quieras, pero recuerda que éstas sirven de respaldo a tu historia, esta comunidad no es de fotografía, por lo que publicar 20 fotos y 100 palabras, no es tan interesante para una guía de viajes. Por otro lado compartir solo 3 imágenes que no resalten aquel increíble viaje tampoco está contando mucho sobre tu aventura. Por lo tanto, una recomendación básica sería incluir al menos 5 fotos del entorno que visitamos, mostrando el paisaje, el pueblo, o los monuments. Hacernos fotos durante el recorrido, selfies, fotos de la comida y el alojamiento es súper agradable de ver, pero no puede ser la parte principal del material audiovisual, recuerda que la comunidad se centra en el destino del viajero. Trata de cuidar la calidad de las fotografías. La falta de enfoque y el inclinarlas, sin buscar dinamismo o cualquier otra forma de expresión artística, acaban en imágenes difíciles de entender. En cuanto a **los vídeos, independientemente de su duración, no se justifica la falta de texto e imágenes** compartiendo nuestra experiencia. No todo el mundo tiene tiempo de ver un vídeo entero, lo mejor es ofrecer al espectador las dos opciones, para que no sólo tengamos visualizaciones del vídeo, sino que invitemos a los lectores a disfrutar de nuestra experiencia. Te recomendamos orientar el dispositivo utilizado para la grabación en horizontal, para que sea más amigable a la vista en 3Speak. ### Fuentes, citas, derechos y créditos Hemos hecho hincapié en la importancia de compartir contenido original, basado en la experiencia personal y de acuerdo con las reglas 3 y 4 de la comunidad, por lo que puede que no haga falta decir que el texto, las imágenes y otros recursos utilizados en la publicación deben ser propios. Sin embargo, en ocasiones puntuales dentro del post, cuando compartamos una imagen o vídeo **autorizado** por terceros, deberemos dar crédito a los autores y enlazar al link de la fuente para comprobar su veracidad. Esto no es un problema si no basamos todo nuestro artículo en la referencia de otra persona, sino que introducimos un elemento para mejorar la historia que hemos compartido con los demás. ### Etiquetas En todo momento, las etiquetas en Hive deben estar relacionadas con el contenido sobre el que escribes. Dentro de la comunidad, no exigimos ninguna en particular, pero #Travel te ayudará a clasificar tu contenido, haciéndolo más accesible cuando alguien se interese por este tema. Lo mismo ocurre cuando incluyes en las etiquetas la ciudad, el país o la región que estás visitando. También puedes utilizar referencias a la forma de viajar, #backpacking, #roadtrip, #solotravel, #hiking, entre otras. Algunos monumentos o características relevantes del lugar visitado son #beach, #nature, #forest, #mountain, #lake. Sólo para facilitar la búsqueda de contenidos similares, en caso de que alguien se interese por el artículo debido a esa mención concreta. En definitiva, aquí buscamos compartir nuestra pasión por viajar: #wanderlust. Si incluyes un idioma que no sea el inglés, utiliza la etiqueta de tu idioma de origen y alguna referencia a los viajes (por ejemplo, #spanish, #viajes, #senderismo #deutsch). ![Foto autorizada por @louis88](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EpvhuUYiyc9pAWJeemu1ss6qhkNptprFMgLr5LDuNr4KGWC9YLjkQxZGjS57ReLovws.jpeg) # Compromiso Por último, tan importante como todos los apartados anteriores, es fundamental el compromiso de cada usuario dentro de la blockchain y especialmente en la comunidad. Si esperamos recibir apoyo, lo más razonable es apoyar a los creadores de contenido que hacen el mismo esfuerzo que nosotros y que dan vida a nuestro universo viajero. Ser un miembro activo de una comunidad no significa sólo publicar en ella, sino interactuar con otros usuarios en las publicaciones de la comunidad más allá de responder a los comentarios de nuestros posts. Votar, comentar y aportar opiniones son formas de apoyarnos mutuamente, compartir experiencias, ponernos en contacto, hacer nuevas amistades y, por supuesto, aprender y añadir valor real al ecosistema. <div class="text-justify">

Good evening, my friends, wherever you are. I hope you are all healthy and happy so you can go about your daily activities as usual. I hope you all have a pleasant day.

In this blog, I want to share some images with you all related to one of the tourist destinations I've also shared in my previous blog, *Seulawah RG Nature Tourism*. However, in this blog, we will focus on exploring and seeing the facilities at that destination.

So, keep following my blog to see the Seulawah Agam RG tourist destination, along with short articles from me.

![IMG-20260420-WA0008.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdxovqGMbXf7Na9BPyQvQxFVNgT6J1XVWqCFGR4aPZrWk/IMG-20260420-WA0008.jpg)

Located in Makmur Village, Blang Bintang District, Aceh Besar Regency, Seulawah RG Nature Tourism Destination is a relatively new tourist destination known for its pristine natural scenery and is a great place to unwind and enjoy a peaceful atmosphere with friends or family.

![IMG-20260420-WA0006.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUYLtefchxuedgAU26A7B4XPUsyB9YtHDh1ZQumMiyBzX/IMG-20260420-WA0006.jpg)

The first thing that caught my attention as I explored this tourist destination was the strikingly colored, love-shaped building perched atop a hill.

My friend...
After I researched the area and arrived, I discovered that this striking building was one of the VIP villas located within the area.
However, on sunny days, this area is often used by visitors as a photo spot, with its stunning views, especially since the building is situated at the highest point of the area, surrounded by synthetic grass.

Now, for those of us who enjoy fishing, you can rest assured that this place also offers a fishing platform with a super-abundance of fish.

Therefore, I highly recommend those of you who enjoy fishing, if you visit here, try to catch some really, really big fish, if you're lucky.

![IMG-20260420-WA0009.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPUiYw1dXBKJ5ReSU2AQC2nPq4TMJjjmQGvkaxLfVfbAf/IMG-20260420-WA0009.jpg)

While fishing, you can also order food, as there's a food service station next to the pond. I think the light snacks available in the area are a perfect way to enjoy the fishing atmosphere while fishing.

Furthermore, the area is very spacious, with more than one food service station.

![IMG-20260420-WA0012.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSj73zB38y2uor9XRvkeFp9pqrr322jqhQpmktufTXQMJ/IMG-20260420-WA0012.jpg)

Another facility I encountered while exploring this tourist destination was a playground.

My friends...
So, for those of you visiting with your beloved children, don't worry, because this place also provides children's play facilities and a wide selection of games.

![IMG-20260420-WA0019.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTkAjzq9AVyUxArKe75VzsZu1CDS2k8VzgeaVGW3aLcox/IMG-20260420-WA0019.jpg)

Okay, my friends, those are some pictures of the facilities at the Seulawah RG nature tourism site.

From that, I can say that not all places can provide a sense of calm with adequate facilities, but this place is different. Here, the atmosphere, views, and feelings blend perfectly.
For me, this isn't just a hangout spot; it's more like a place to reset.
Therefore, I highly recommend that you all consider visiting the Seulawah RG nature tourism site if you're ever in Aceh.

And thank you very much to all of you who have taken the time to view and read my blog to the end.
Leave your comments, support, and input, which means a lot to me, so I can make this blog even better in the future.

That's all for now.
Greetings everyone.
See you in my next blog.

Liebe Müll-Produzenten,
wer in Wien zum ersten Mal mit der U4 oder U6 an der Station Spittelau vorbeikommt, trifft auf ein überrasched buntes Gebäude, das so gar nicht nach Industrieanlage aussieht — Türme, goldene Kugeln, unregelmäßige Fassaden in Gelb, Blau und Rot und Bäume am Dach. Man könnte meinen, hier wurde ein weiteres [Hundertwasserhaus](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hundertwasserhaus_(Wien)) errichtet. Was sich dahinter verbirgt, ist eine ganz gewöhnliche Müllverbrennungsanlage — oder doch nicht so gewöhnlich.

Blick vom Norden, von der Heiligenstädterbrücke über den Donaukanal.
![IMG_4326.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/242rtshbry5wD4Xi4uGAg9pBYhX1MSJh6hBswLUEdqSWRt9Cm7rsAivgVcsHurGCe7tHv.jpg)
Die beiden Türme rechts im Hintergrund gehören zum [AKH](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allgemeines_Krankenhaus_der_Stadt_Wien), einem der größten Spitäler Europas, für deren Energieversorgung die ca. 2km entfernte Spittelau erst gebaut wurde. 

##### Von der nüchternen Zweckanlage zum Wahrzeichen
Die Anlage, offiziell "Thermische Abfallbehandlung Spittelau" genannt, wurde 1969-1971 von Simmering-Graz-Pauker errichtet, ein schlichter Industriebau, der seinen Zweck erfüllte und weiter nichts. 1987 zerstörte ein Brand große Teile der Anlage. Statt sie abzureißen, entschied die Stadt Wien, sie neu aufzubauen — und dabei etwas Außergewöhnliches zu wagen. Der Beharrlichkeit des damaligen Wiener Bürgermeisters Helmut Zilk (dessen Porträt heute im Stadtsenats-Sitzungssaal des [Rathauses](https://peakd.com/hive-166496/@stayoutoftherz/das-wiener-rathaus-viennas-city-hall) hängt) ist es zu verdanken, dass [Friedensreich Regentag Dunkelbunt Hundertwasser](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedensreich_Hundertwasser) die Umgestaltung übernahm (1988-1992).
Denn Hundertwasser war zuerst alles andere als begeistert: Er lehnte das Projekt aus ökologischen Gründen ab — er wollte nicht etwas verschönern, das der Natur schadet. Letztendlich stimmte er unter drei Bedingungen zu: modernste Filteranlagen, niemand sollte sich in seine Pläne einmischen, und er arbeitete unentgeltlich. So konnte niemand ihn beschuldigen, an einem „schmutzigen" Thema zu verdienen.

Der Vergleich vorher-nachher aus einem Video, das vor der eigentlichen Führung gezeigt wird.
![IMG_4488.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/243BYGdfvr5kdrD6ksu7Ay91QK2GTYAryw2qamcTymd67aZaxrG7ecWCD65VF3byWDMZd.jpg)
---

Hier werden *täglich* (montags bis freitags) von rund 200 Müllwägen ca. 670 Tonnen Hausmüll abgeladen, im Jahr summiert sich das auf rund 250.000 Tonnen! Ein unangenehmer Geruch liegt in der Luft, aber das war klar bei so viel Müll🤕. 
![IMG_4497.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/EqQP3VznY8xwW8RhAPxn2H48mT8H3SdVQuw7EQL6MB4gkG3HCqMYcdqt5nJDyRDX3x5.jpg)

Um die Ecke (am oberen Foto nicht zu sehen, hinter dem weißen PKW rechts) ein kurioses kleines Häuschen - ein WC für die Müllwagenfahrer 😄!
![IMG_4543.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/23wX1Fzk7Fuuoz5Jvaeor9JKcn2RqivBTiFAwo12C9qeh67E2by2nDdaZCu7KHqbdxrF9.jpg)


##### Wie funktioniert moderne Müllverbrennung?

Der Müll landet in einem riesigen Sammelbecken, "Bunker" genannt. Die Besucher sind zum Glück durch Glasscheiben vom Müllberg getrennt. Oben erkennt man die zwei Öffnungen (die linke ist großteils nicht zu sehen), durch die der Müll mit zwei riesigen Polypenkränen, manuell gesteuert, aus dem Bunker in die zwei Heizkessel befördert wird. Die laufen 24/7. Nur einmal im Jahr wird ausgeschaltet für die jährliche Wartung. 
![IMG_4530.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/23wCDgRDiTTtn3tKtbzEeMoi5xSJD5LQdPPKZE2S7bGdLtRnWB8kHu94vtWWm7uSHHaQy.jpg)

![IMG_4529.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/23xepPusWD5LTnd9MqgCpPLvF148ReuKKpFABWqU6tX6uNeybLjSdnYUbHrYrbgW38yrZ.jpg)

Die Kräne verfrachten den Müll nicht nur in die Heizkessel, sondern packen immer wieder Müll und lassen ihn wieder los. Kein Versehen, sondern Absicht. Nur so kann gewährleistet werden, dass größere Gegenstände wie Fahrräder vorher erkannt und aussortiert werden. Die würden nämlich sonst die Einlasstricher der Kessel verstopfen. Alles, was nicht aussortiert wird, landet in den Heizkesseln und wird mind. 1h bei 850 Grad C. verbrannt, was angeblich die allermeisten Giftstoffe zerstört.

Teil der Heizkesselanlage. In die anderen Bereiche der Anlage (Turbinen, Fernkälteerzeugung, etc.) konnte man leider nicht gelangen.
![IMG_4503.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/EoK6mBggibVeLRvgSYzCjgzvi2oY712RymCtHgaq5DTzfWNmuL6kuA2xR1j6ji8jZAF.jpg)


Und nach der Verbrennung? Es entstehen dabei ca. 20% Schlacke und 2,5% Asche, d.h. ja 200kg und 25kg pro Tonne Hausmüll. Die Schlacke und die Asche werden mit Wasser und Zement gebunden zu Schlackenzement (im Bild unten). Der ist ziemlich inert und kann für Straßenfundamentierungen genutzt werden.
![IMG_4538.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/23yncnSEtB1xHS3xeUxo7jkr48CRpGKEh7VPdCQi3h7wBd4kPF1Cz9VnzLDyp9DjxXQMJ.jpg)

Was natürlich noch entsteht, sind die flüchtigen Verbrennungsprodukte, also die Abgase. Die werden zuerst durch (teure, aber wieder verwendbare) Gewebefilter geleitet, siehe die Röhre im unteren Bild. Danach kommt eine sog. Rauchgaswäsche, bei der die übrigen Partikel, auch Feinstaub, in Wasser gebunden werden. Das Wasser wird gereinigt und dem Kreislauf wieder zugeführt. Die heißen Abgase werden für Fernwärme genutzt. Am Schluss durchlaufen die Abgase noch eine katalytische DeNO<sub>x</sub>-Anlage zum Abbau von Dioxinen und Stickoxiden (die "Entstickung" gibt es seit 1991 in dieser Form und war damals weltweit eine der ersten). Der Rest gelangt über den Schlot in die Luft.
Angeblich ist das, was dort oben rauskommt, sauberer als die Luft ringsherum auf Straßenniveau (also das, was wir tagtäglich einatmen), da z.B. der allgegenwärtige Feinstaub (Gummiabrieb von Fahrzeugen, Hausbrand, etc.) nicht mehr enthalten ist!
![IMG_4536.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/23wMct3tfsYn598urA4dQwCVmnBFh67F9FtzjNZ72tKfZ4fizZYLAsG5X7NxiNGyvoKqD.jpg)
Übrig nach der Abgasbehandlung bleibt ein hochgiftiger, schwermetallreicher Filterkuchen - 0,1% des Mülls (1kg pro Tonne). Der wird in einer Spezialdeponie in Deutschland endgelagert, im stillgelegten Salzbergwerk Heilbronn - dort lagern bereits 160.000 Tonnen Müllrückstände aus Wien!

Mit der Wärme aus der Verbrennung werden ca. 60.000 Wiener Haushalte mit Energie versorgt (inkl. Warmwasser) und ca. 50.000 Wiener Haushalte mit Strom. Seit 2009 wird hier auch Fern*kälte* produziert.
Nicht ganz so bekannt: In der Spittelau lässt die Polizei mehrmals wöchentlich Schmuggelware vernichten — Zigaretten, Cannabis und Kokain gehen so in Fernwärme über ([Quelle](https://www.moderne-regional.de/fachbeitrag-muellverbrennungsanlage-spittelau/)).

##### Das Gebäude
Westfassade. Rund um die Fenster sind oft Ausmalungen in der Größe einer Armlänge - Hunderwasser nannte das ["Fensterrecht"](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fensterrecht).
![IMG_4484.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/23yTYt3c5SFiWdDfannvRjCmRZPTWtAuZSeXG197LSPpmZE1YnNR2QLT26ND3SywvsYLf.jpg)

Der 126m hohe Abgasschlot. Die große goldene Kugel (die eigentlich eine Zwiebel darstellt!) ist vor allem dekorativ, es gibt dort keine Aussichtsplattform oder ein Kaffeehaus (was genial wäre), nur eine Messstation zur Abgasmessung. Die Abgaswerte kann man [hier](https://www.wienenergie.at/ueber-uns/unternehmen/energie-klimaschutz/energieerzeugung/abfallverwertungsanlagen/emissionswerte/) einsehen.
![IMG_4482.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/242NWCd1592XdiU1GcSR6pkuHXSs92pE9pE6XbxWNSSGUo1opdcEGkv2MrD5qUwBMZkCo.jpg)

Unter dem obersten goldenen Ring sind Löcher zu erkennen. Dort nisten Turmfalken!
![IMG_4499.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/2432HqZm1UPE1vdd53jLPoK5L2va1NYoDu8gj1Eb2HR3ann7fLFJiFQoG34WJPFiygvFE.jpg)

Auf einem der begrünten Dächer. Vor ein paar Jahren mussten die Bäumen (nach 35 Jahren) gefällt werden und durch kleinere ersetzt werden, da die Statik sonst gefährdet gewesen wäre.
![IMG_4506.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/EpnCk9hmzXH5TMydrzzYXdixqQJ1162jjhtbCxGoMnQ5BY91sQG6Ep2WVHt9o9E1Puv.jpg)

Das Verwaltungsgebäude neben der Verbrennungsanlage wurde ebenfalls verziert, mit Kugeln, roten "Lebensadern" und dem obligatorischen begrünten Dach.
![IMG_4509.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/244KLTdMGMVeHJGQGaVimHCEGL52WvXhKh2PM1gXoKXTNQnF4FGdNuJdY1hr1xPVEUFy1.jpg)


##### Das Kapperl
![IMG_4525.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/243Bko8qUTtWtStJhBzqgLVCGAFFWQNkWxmAxxquy4us4FfGSfHV6mtxPhAu7PywVxSRk.jpg)

Eine der amüsantesten Geschichten rund um die Spittelau betrifft das auffällige Metallkapperl auf einem Lüftungsschacht. Um diesen entbrannte eine Diskussion, wie er am besten dekoriert werden könnte (eine Kugel wäre zu groß). Als man sich partout nicht einigen konnte, verlor Hundertwasser die Geduld und verließ zornig die Runde mit den Worten „Ich hau den Hut drauf!" — eine österreichischen Redewendung für Aufgeben. Die Bauherren nahmen ihn beim Wort und ergänzten die Anlage tatsächlich um besagtes Kapperl, für das Hundertwasser berühmt war, weil er es fast immer trug (er hatte es selbst genäht, denn er war auch ein guter Schneider).
![IMG_4524.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/242DNom745J4bvfTNZoo1PiuZfLCqnwodTWRrxbynfYhq4hps3hMppVY5wdwfzyNiS2TQ.jpg)
Links im Hintergrund der Kahlenberg.

Blick vom Dach über den Donaukanal auf die Brigittenau (20. Bezirk Wiens). Man sieht rechts der Bildmitte 2 der insg. 6 [Flak-Türme](https://peakd.com/deutsch/@stayoutoftherz/about-the-flak-towers-in-vienna-die-flak-tuerme-in-wien) (ziemlich genau in deren Mitte weiter hinten das Riesenrad). Rechts vom rechten Flakturm sind die beiden 200m hohen Schlote des Kraftwerks Simmering zu sehen, des größten Kraftwerks Österreichs, das bei Vollast 50% der Wiener Haushalte mit Strom versorgen kann. Aber das ist eine andere Geschichte...
![IMG_4519.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/stayoutoftherz/Eq9VLxNFNuWhtH3tuzVKP95pZfd9BHGm5ndgmZgbjXbpHTSCWXtKYeewjo1Y3Lxgv6v.jpg)

Am besten ist natürlich **Abfallvermeidung**! Je weniger Hausmüll entsteht, umso weniger davon muss  aufwendig entsorgt werden!
Zuletzt noch eine Frage: Wohin mit Pizzakartons, Restmüll oder Altpapier? Was meint Ihr?

Las iglesias siempre tienen un toque misterioso no se a mi me parece eso, no se si a otros les sucede, pero lo que también puedo ver es que me recuerdan a esas épocas de la Colonia, me recuerdan a pueblo y a personas con necesidad de buscar un poco de espiritualidad; esta iglesia fue fundada en 1879 y remodelada en el 2025 cuando reabrió sus puertas al público en general, fue remodelada por dentro y por fuera, preservando su estilo barroco. A la iglesia le sustituyeron el techo completo, todo de madera, al entrar se logra ver la profundidad del mismo que son como bovedas y ahora tienen unos ventiladores para refrescar un poco a todos aquellos feligreses que llegan a este santuario, aquí también hay algunas pinturas religiosas y las grandes columnas y algunos retablos dorados que transportan al pasado y dejam ver como hay un aire de majetuosidad que recuerdan las riquezas. Cada detalle a la entrada de la iglesia y dentro de ella son dignos de admirar, la entrada tiene dos puertas grandes, con pequeñas puntas doradas que llaman la atención y las columnas blancas grandes y con toques dorados invitan a admirar la belleza arquitectónica que ha sido creada con tanto esmero. Esta es la iglesia principal de cagua y al entrar pude ver algunas personas que van rezar según sus creencias y a pedir con fe, algo que siempre me ha llamado la atención es que estas iglesias grandes y principales siempre están abiertas y eso es bueno porque muchas personas recurren allí en cualquier momento en busca de consuelo y pueden encontrarlo. Las bancas son de maderas, de esas antiguas que se pueden ver hasta en las películas, pero es bonito ver cosas de épocas, las columnas y arcos que aquí se encuentran hacen una decoración especial para darle un toque perfecto a esta iglesia, los arcos tienen unos bordes que llaman mucho la atención, están como en relieve, y en medio del arco una lámpara y en las paredes existen varias figuras representativas eclesiásticas que dan armonía y espiritualidad al lugar. Me pareció que el podio o la parte principal es bastante sencilla, pero me llamo mucho la atención cuando iba saliendo es que en la puerta principal en la parte de arriba hay una especie de terraza que ve hacia el frente, y aunque no se parecía muy bien en la foto hay como una ventaba vitral, se ve muy bonito, este fue mi pequeño recorrido por esta iglesia de San José de Cagua.

And the last but not the last post about my fall stay in Lasko, Slovenia, is finally here. Although I have written about this place before, every visit there is a new and unique experience and the photos are always very inspiring.

![IMG_20251108_121109.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqL9gt87j9wzXorHaSRBX8vK4mMzD52o1KPbmx1wJPsfxHMsCqT5qGpuMZaVUz8xgZH.jpg)

My last trip there was in November for my son's birthday. Our daily walk through the Savinja River valley was wrapped in deep autumn colors, leaves and the soft sound of water moving beside us.

![IMG_20251108_115409.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqWnFcs2uYvNvtTVE9miSrbfByxXgy9FW2Q1EQzT2azYZJWMt8y11rEvnRuv79dk6su.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_113636.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep3dPzP8B3YfjtYBaixaNJmvwoS4hnpRPkGW3nYA9PtvJAryDCWaxFFr8BStBr72z21.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_121103.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpvjNDsaVbkdAPnQXmRXKBBjVtr1fHztSpxXdMbsikmqAutFxKKeAJ2qWnXFkiWjs3i.jpg)

It was one of those slow moments where you don't check your phone, just breathe and look around.

![IMG_20251108_132933.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep7u9xgU2qEqVpEU4nP8v7KBNDGShQ6n8ccyJBcxGrt8KWNM9TQhvfwkaoUZJd2y6gW.jpg)

We stopped at a small restaurant where, unexpectedly, art meets comfort.

![IMG_20251108_123557.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eou9eUTyYo43VN8GLFQeJL26Zf2aBbPvLdRooGc7imejPBwzjp2mJYrb5FmiA5ZoUKP.jpg)

An exhibition of local bird pictures was impressive. This is the place of the most diverse birds.

![IMG_20251108_123527.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoErU5GvQjb8zuUaeiyYQPG9BYpXa7tmmSUveJoHtd2cp6UJ17vQx4GUrPG7Udjjt3h.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123549.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpCAvv9iaRW9vtEzTLsV3m1p2EesaoWGbiHGgKdkZPvz9p2seB2TUhfgepkLNC2y7T5.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123533.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eos1kKDRdiqYSLV2iUqv1ME5GXMnuS9137UbjHVcPkb6dYojii6mZ5m8ybfm7KSAR2H.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123510.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep5o6yAnabnbyz9eG6AE3QFyGsu9EedrEnMdEC2XdfoeMzqgkjPFSdU9kuuwoui859n.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123541.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoeFovDcxbt6m6pZsZzENV2yYw6iKBJHqvi7M4c5uarz9pNvgg3A1F1Ksh1FvBEfGX9.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123522.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoGypRbtcBkjZrp96VwYdao7bE4mMYwEqHPrCDep9UB2QvLE9HV5qeoSjPcxCtC4CRW.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123552.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eou9DyP821afv7pNPceTSyVhYPhZ6BZEGSc8g3ZmMupyGqg5emssdH5m3NpmoFbsqB1.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123606.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EogPLCtxc89BjPS7NdKkX5zBUe1gvFqmKmQzjvuh2NWzxpFDSD9bFv5wLLJRfLVqB6G.jpg)

It made the place feel more personal, almost like being invited into someone's story, with Lasko beer that always pleases, whatever the season. 

![IMG_20251108_122617.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/23xKvnKP1wi2md75MPDvsKzLgihFRgA5NTtQcY1BYiFm7jhjKuXcHyifTmDaPkX748jnP.jpg)

And the burgers were just as always simple, rich, and exactly what you want after a long walk.

![IMG_20251108_123650.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EonnPa23wwSneWarG2dENHPENs99UihispH2X2a6hSi8uR1pq4rt4D3v5bTGGmzSErG.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123643.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EogPmfWJRL8mK3A1Ru2aLkB6ee8tN1w4HHvD31tsY2N1Np7GFdgVwB9FWv6rsmSJ3my.jpg)

We were again accommodated in the Termana Park hotel, and the view from the hotel room of the Savinja River amazed me again and again every morning.

![IMG_20251108_133341.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqNG4n1mn3nguFVB5ye8kHcgSSx29u4ReuexNMdprB6NJE6wuprZ3B9ZD2CdEEhBYCQ.jpg)

Morning light reflected on the water, making everything feel calm as the fog moved up.

![IMG_20251109_100716.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpJY7CSPkgnkjZfVpnoG9qse3vyg2B95sAUi878Hoq9GjM1dxaTeqLv9JvcnRkySUya.jpg)

![IMG_20251109_100720.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpEGJQDhRe2FtEKiqaDR3UrTanrRN4DH2i8MZJjVGZ4M28kPrQw6hdnWurmtATsczez.jpg)

![IMG_20251109_100724.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpNnpnmPFXi5HJy7JLJ3s2GyVQZMFfxdLMe9pP5YzQfjBeUFrdja4kid2WskRkHm3WP.jpg)

And bathing in the thermal waters of this place was, as always, the best experience, at least for me. 😊 

![IMG_20251108_170120.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoJyZKhm6Cj7TFASrCBjkMRrqXz8xuJ59U6wf2KNUaXKwWf2XJAabcDBvTT42Kwky2q.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_180753.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoK3xLmkEYV4yiEb83aCVwVZf3vMbu5Cx1bGJEpFEirV9xAJadE5WhRTPaev2ZCH2vU.jpg)

![IMG_20251109_180613.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eoc556VtZCQjdn4ofCbZHQHx5i4JSqaUh1muLKFHXyFW5oMoMBQGx8rf7Fbgk4FJXiy.jpg)

![IMG_20251109_180606.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EorxwGRXgqT3q6TW2HrtBiA3rMRXE3VBtShpY1ikRufmbXCgFmsXU1zUQfX76jLExpY.jpg)

Moving between the indoor and outdoor thermal pools, surrounded by cool November air, was the highlight.

![IMG_20251110_143350.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoGwwKkLuPupUHXVnjdZadw2x6UyaetaEryLrzGzrAYa5TbMJRQGxHTkVtuaTJ88ZCJ.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_142755.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpzvJcvkNSFt5Fiy7aXPejofx8FYcmB5tVRvodb4gZ6o9zPBaE7j5fcL9mSFJbDUQ39.jpg)

Warm water, silence, and that contrast between seasons... it's a feeling worth repeating.

I love the places I go back to.

![4i88GgaV8qiFkxbnGCXnHPUK3daVLCQA4oDc4iy6ghu2vJQJmmeoVEo8rvajHaCCkUyqJATNCMc48vtE83mAWqDQJEkMdBPfjJVFfd4oyRFTSogDiDskgQcJut.webp](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoGvUz9hKnnCbtpUM2j1FJdAutJrrz3gZ4rmwugVpGJkqiKwUMv715DrsSZo7inCi8x.webp)

Thank you for reading.

Jelena

ENGLISH VERSION (click here!) Hello travelers, happy Tuesday to everyone. ![InShot_20260420_074705550.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EpGSAryA71BLdnZhrC2RAZuHQQuaQroJtwXh86DdybQXxahkcB2n84dBhv792e63gy9.jpg) We left the San Isidro Labrador Chapel behind and continued along a long path up a steep hill leading to the Monument of the Virgin of Peace. The monument is surrounded by green grass, beautiful trees, and flowers, filling visitors with a sense of harmony and well-being thanks to such beautiful landscapes that seem straight out of a fairy tale. ![20260402_132646.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EnugvvQ3o5H1DmpLQPavnKia7f2XZwwnxmKptZccVSn5xoqmTbEU6nAKS6qdSRqTexw.jpg) ![20260402_132656.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/Eoc6YwvzAYsHq8H79kAYCTRHS8Z8aB8fpx44K9NdEhc5YWqyJZm9yUgMDF27Adj8E5p.jpg) ![20260402_132838.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/Eou7iXj8vUCeka4D5bAeYB3CNWa1zNMhJE7HtxyvPB7be9rzjgfd5amVdbq1c1cjMzm.jpg) ![20260402_132816.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EnugWbZVbwyf5cxvZTHhRrhF6TM7bsAngoEcirBAyc1CyXhSFxCqv4VW6JF1MNtzinA.jpg) ![20260402_132825.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EqQM9XSySSfvAvdwhz3MyjjYiKuhgwyXVuqwLWaZNtN2d8ZHZuZWEGFoC8d7WLLoyNQ.jpg) ![20260402_132932.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EoTayFkSQZB5f9qvgcJKWpNy3vh6c9pUQf2jdfooAMvJ3sq1nejvMMf2C6JvHCfgKHq.jpg) ![20260402_133019.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EpnBPy9KyZxVq5zWi4UNpxzyJ4WM4vXytCRR1J1A4GHFui8oWNvTzjd48vFwP9duBqJ.jpg) ![20260402_133947.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EnugyfH3k8BwhLpxCMj8wrLUy9obAV5PVokENhm7ptamxZpEpnPvaoKDay5xs9W1j7d.jpg) We were getting closer and closer to the Peace Monument, which was partially shrouded in mist. Before getting any closer to it, I could see the tiny houses that make up the state capital of Trujillo. I was so happy to be there—I hadn’t been since I was 13—and that moment brought back endless memories of spending vacations there with my family. I’m eagerly looking forward to the day I can bring my girls there. ![20260402_132916.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EnmBK5SajE3D12QZ7yxcHZRWFer8zSJtYNHCvXYoYY53X8qcpqhqzHHQVsG1Ztvugwr.jpg) ![20260402_133126.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EnqTYEwgYWbfD7ZK81eg7T23gtEbfazcB6skACAhMQabcXAuVZHwBDz1wxBQ6GcSRH1.jpg) ![20260402_133259.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EpVB7BSdHGi1iTr8g1oBdbyLSVpRLFWa9LFmbuz7u4myY7c22Vfn2aghHCD5QVwXSwa.jpg) ![20260402_133100.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EpxqDs6nxhH5SK9fFXouGdLPYTeKoxkwgYK88U45Qz5LsVugsgocNrFfURf4cY1tcpG.jpg) We reached the base of the monument, and just as we were about to climb up, we decided to grab a bite to eat instead, because there was a huge line of people waiting to go up. we turned back and took another path, one lined with pine trees, their scent filling the air. Nearby was a park where children could play, and further on we found a wishing well where there were some bills and coins at the bottom; a small sculpture of the Virgin of Peace stood out. ![20260402_133848.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EnaYLBnALLCAzDPziAmvGC6iw14eMKb7SoRuDW46A6EGMvDnck5vA1KVvmq5P1hD6tJ.jpg) ![20260402_133954.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EpLf4rY1qJx5EJUETk3xDCG2GZZWsoMgro5DNC831QjAHEC6q19Y8PbZF5Fyh2m3QoA.jpg) ![20260402_134311.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EqfFR5x3UGqGeVo2qwMHNQQVJnMrSgjd7DuKNhmQdVsDGULpxnF9eNCp73d51u6Jg2u.jpg ![20260402_134325.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/Eq7KydQo9hHxRkM2DqZvymRuUW92EqJF76bWzr6X2QwzJttf48cssfAT3BteXvoJkx8.jpg) ![20260402_134454.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EpT3Ch8oGw1P9fGk3p5itoTNy375gkucC92X1VFqxP1BqtDBGRjeT2dtaUz4hZGvyRj.jpg) ![20260402_134458.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EpGPpEP4576dRSykpHRXjvzswTF4dboE1NAC574CykMuXTnc4Lvp39rzRoe18ipSxKj.jpg) ![20260402_134325.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/Eq7KydQo9hHxRkM2DqZvymRuUW92EqJF76bWzr6X2QwzJttf48cssfAT3BteXvoJkx8.jpg) ![20260402_134527.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EoK5RDvPuoUN4fuhGiktCVMK5KA8DMyCXGSEQnuYKDMMLQne1CdJND3HuVWdXK5yG6s.jpg) While Ricardo and I were looking for something to eat, we came across a little house for elves in a tree trunk. Remember that they are the protectors of nature, and in the state of Trujillo they are called Momoy. ![20260402_134724.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EoiVj4w1L27qbJp4iPL9sBYDJQSXBf8Qfv8J4QSrtfAvhACJinrW2uRKwF7y7FodQnx.jpg) ![20260402_134758.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EorzMQ4FBmiSwdJdBKTDmw7xweU21GBTgWfmPPWF7Wxz9KFt7Zfov37bekDtEARqBGA.jpg) We found a place to eat; a bowl of shelled corn which would be our lunch and a small glass of juice cost $2. It was delicious and came with sour cream, fresh cheese, and yellow cheese. We were happy with our choice and took the opportunity to buy a fridge magnet. ![IMG-20260420-WA0009.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EpQuqVRo63qziCPNPzVDnd3TsGQ1CTkVDqiXdiXeCJ5VS7wzCbYiwjoYX7ZYfWpVAVe.jpg) ![20260402_135308.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EoCi8PDNTWgUV9YnxdBBf2LMsxezztVBSfVM2yAkU7ieSTG2PZ35WNAdSa9iTda1Lvd.jpg) We went back to the monument, and the line was still long, but it didn't matter because we weren't hungry anymore, so we were able to wait patiently for about 20 minutes until it was our turn. ![20260402_142110.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EpVA6kbfqaaYr8hV4LctnmWxgctH2uyFhQfJsBQyJrxX7zGk4bY64tkwXdb746d7Azc.jpg) ![20260402_140457.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/Eq9Uk6j873nu8s1VrnMQMmMss5H2B4PkyUWRiedwA7jDQpaDEECRDPAxcAW2zZUULuN.jpg) ![20260402_141502.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EogMpdsLFFhkdTuLaLWYd4vz6RB1yD32eudV8cikJEioM4rwZwU3VkSivJD76jdNWvL.jpg) We reached the base of the mountain, which is about 18 meters high. From there, we could see the beautiful, majestic mountains touching the sky, and we could also see the people waiting to climb up. ![20260402_142310.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EpC9tY1oqc9CTx8ZzszQGwSRWYwwHGuC3MmxT3E99uzt47rxef9EfadqbwZ8rCT1SoA.jpg) ![20260402_142351.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EprSCLy8kG97KnA7L2vQahPZXHdfHXyBbq6HDFqhqVrzUVVRgU6UtoFFKYCMh6dr7wM.jpg) ![20260402_142319.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EoXrfJMhX6wTLHvaQFCxyAVv495fPWyJ7yYRug5HjFqzYvcHoAKi9Nc6frnqPb2nYF4.jpg) ![20260402_142314.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EnYQRdSRvSRYHxdfaStv28xYScTZAVyNfPhrC8fNAN3rTqFWWE4CU6tqjNEUYpzEBaW.jpg) ![20260402_142328.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EnYQuv7zX9MB61r7FAogNMWp7svx7H5dx27chtMbJN2NFQGt2uwTaq68XhTabd8coiB.jpg) Between the steps, at 22 meters, is the left hand; from here I could feel closer to the sky. A few steps later, at 26 meters, was the right hand, where the Virgin holds the dove of peace. The panoramic view was spectacular. At this point, I was more scared and didn’t want to keep climbing, so I just looked up and could see her face. We decided not to climb any further, but I felt happy to have made it past the halfway point of the monument. ![20260402_142608.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/Ep3dpZ33mu6V9MvB2bzRRzVGxgY4CP8hisK71o38wBwp8a4w2cEYg5ubqEcnjrpeuCK.jpg) ![20260402_142524.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EnaYNv7Jpb77J49q2Cd1PjyDNv6dtYBo7e3cSZSnDSoSqPQ7umktkLGPTrBBFpBB9rV.jpg) ![20260402_142515.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EppKDd5rojHG4fBV62kyPgVvSWyDtJVKJGFMs23BKQHV2MyeSarP2EjH8nxuDcrEsdJ.jpg) ![20260402_142622.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/Epzwp6ayCmCPLhaGQpYjZbYkpQAXHRyyvexiyERbexjqHRiQakdHaVndAjYwJubwCLF.jpg) ![20260402_142722.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EnaYr8P5PkHm6UBodvPXV7CQ2Dr7mwMEY2d8qj7CLyAicVZNtVXAgrCBuYVB3doKoTm.jpg) ![20260402_142728.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EpA1Uats4rdXBhVAufJKAX9emxqiVacTTUUshQdKvHG7EZjjqy7roTUfDzE7eKPPtgL.jpg) Finally, we descended and said goodbye to the largest monument in the Americas, and we were able to get a clear view of the Virgin of Peace from afar—what a source of pride that she is located in my beautiful Venezuela. ![20260402_151743.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/noalys/EpGPHCpiThnxBGd6VfJ5oorsnDUaBj9m4dbNwYPzzav1xB4gHgJvsAtZmQCBXo57LPT.jpg)

Hello, Fellow Travelers

We often don’t know where waterfalls come from; like a secret pool hidden by the mountains and hills, they are ready to meet the earth when the time comes.  That clear water, breaking free from the heights, flows onward, touching the grass, stones, and moss along the way. Then, reaching a high cliff, it plunges downward. It is at that moment that we witness the most beautiful part of the scenery. Just like the view I saw at the natural wonder of Toparlar Waterfall, located between Köyceğiz and Akyaka...


>Merhaba Gezginci Dostlarım

>Şelalelerin nereden geldiğini çoğu zaman bilmeyiz; sanki dağların ve tepelerin sakladığı gizli bir havuz gibi, zamanı geldiğinde yeryüzüyle buluşmaya hazırdır.  Yükseklerden kopup gelen o berrak su, yol boyunca otlara, taşlara ve yosunlara dokunarak ilerliyor. Sonra yüksek bir kayalığa gelerek kendini aşağıya bırakıyor. İşte o an manzaranın en güzel anına tanıklık ediyoruz.  Tıpkı Köyceğiz ve Akyaka arasında kalan doğa harikası Toparlar Şelalesinde gördüğüm manzara gibi...

[//]:# (!worldmappin 36.99741 lat 28.63294 long  d3scr)

![IMG20260325141806.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcfPp965TcEj74PFgcfmvyBANcBwR8paGbhUJ5SSkExg4/IMG20260325141806.jpg)

While I was on vacation in the Aegean region, I really wanted to see the waterfall located in the Toparlar neighborhood, which is part of the Köyceğiz district in Muğla province. To see the waterfall, which is about 5 km from the Köyceğiz district, I set out from the hotel where I was staying in Ölüdeniz.  To get to the waterfall, I drove from Ölüdeniz along the Fethiye-Muğla road, turned off at the sign for Toparlar Waterfall, and drove about 5 km on a dirt road until I reached a certain point. After that, we reached Toparlar Waterfall following a 10- to 15-minute walk. 

>Ege'de tatil yaptığım sıralarda Muğla ilimizin Köyceğiz ilçesine bağlı olan ve Toparlar Mahallesinde bulunan şelaleyi yakından görmeyi çok istemiştim. Köyceğiz ilçesine yaklaşık 5 km uzaklıkta olan şelaleyi görmek için  Ölüdeniz'de kaldığım otelden yola çıktım.  Şelaleye gitmek için Ölüdeniz'den Fethiye Muğla yolundan ilerleyerek Toparlar Şelalesi yazan tabeledan saparak yaklaşık 5 km topraklı yoldan aracımla belirli bir noktaya kadar geldim. Sonrasında 10 15 dakikalık bir yürüyüşten sonra Toparlar Şelalesine ulaştık. 


![IMG20260325140958.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbyJKoAcm6i8fgTBs7WqP6KYzKb1hW3zuyy2RjyYe9hHU/IMG20260325140958.jpg)

![IMG20260325140954.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYVYL7Q4f97zAaJdZWhi8vaV3eMdiSQ1YBFoMZNyMjQCu/IMG20260325140954.jpg)

![IMG20260325164400.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmW8XTT9L3gFH1pNWrEfkGDn614NGdJZo5HswSBs3Ja8zU/IMG20260325164400.jpg)

![IMG20260325140329.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfXD1BNNnjvixPt99PdrGmJmarxKg7dW4fRQdx3tjDbNz/IMG20260325140329.jpg)

![IMG20260325140353.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVYgAtWAgUBbtzRbYyGMjufJube3avKz7dAJ8fR7zqCcw/IMG20260325140353.jpg)

![IMG20260325140933.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVNb1rqGhsYvSm31q9LmX1UY5t1z5KmQczxsc2CEELWm7/IMG20260325140933.jpg)

The waterfall flows along a stream through a wide forest, winding its way between large and small rocks that have taken on a black hue. We walked along a narrow dirt path at the edge of the stream, and at times along rocky paths where the stream flows, heading straight toward the waterfall.  As we walked along the path, small waterfalls had formed in some sections of the stream. In fact, the water had created depths so great we couldn’t see the bottom. People probably swim here in the summer.  The waterfall flows at its strongest during March, April, and May. During these months, the rushing water has carved out the rocks, forming small pools.  We specifically added this spot to our travel itineraries during these months. Because most waterfalls and streams flow very rapidly during these months due to the combination of melting snow and rainwater. This phenomenon can be observed both along the Mediterranean coast and the Aegean coast. 

>Şelale, geniş bir ormanın içinde siyah rengine bürünmüş irili ufaklı taşların arasından bir dere boyunca akıyor.  Derenin kenarından dar topraklı yoldan ve zaman zaman da akan derenin bulunduğu taşlı yollardan geçerek şelalenin tam aktığı yöne doğru yürüdük.  Yolda yürürken derenin bazı bölümlerinde küçük küçük şelaleler oluşmuş. Hatta suyun dibini göremediğimiz derinlikler oluşturmuş. Muhtemelen yazın buralarda suya giriyorlar.  Mart Nisan ve Mayıs aylarında şelale en güçlü haliyle akıyor. Bu aylarda şiddetli akan sular kayaları da oyarak küçük küçük havuzlar oluşturmuş.  Biz özellikle bu aylarda burayı gezi rotalarımıza ekledik. Çünkü çoğu şelale ve dereler karların erimesiyle   ve  yağmur sularının birleşimiyle bu aylarda çok hızlı akarkar. Bu durum hem Akdeniz kıyılarında hem de Ege kıyılarında görülebiliyor. 

![IMG20260325143005.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmabHvKu9ce5g8PUTRxqPdRWHH4NNdW7UJYyFdMaZjdAkY/IMG20260325143005.jpg)


![IMG20260325140744.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPAxJBziaydCsZHYfBCf6TbysHM1yiQpKcbW7MRZXtaXx/IMG20260325140744.jpg)

![IMG20260325140740.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSh8bNPTR5XBryvTECA7SxaDZVXuRQNHxFV8YuxVq7bkN/IMG20260325140740.jpg)

![IMG20260325140718.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQHpbwN2bkH135W4k8NF5gq9NHogq6yrfLSBTK8NhSv2K/IMG20260325140718.jpg)

We walked along the water’s edge—and sometimes even in the water—toward the point where the waterfall originated. The water looked quite clear and shallow. The fact that the stones were clearly visible and looked so vibrant also showed just how clean the water was. The current wasn’t very strong, but in some sections, the water falling from a height increased its speed.  Amid the sounds of birds and insects, we continued on our way, feeling both the coolness of the water and its soothing calm. Occasionally, we sat on a rock along the edge and focused solely on the sound of the water. Most of the rocks around us had been shaped by the water.  They had all taken on different forms and were scattered about. 

>Suyun kenarından ve bazen de içinde yürüyerek şelalenin geldiği noktaya doğru yürüdük. Su oldukça berrak ve sığ görünüyordu. Taşların net bir şekilde seçilebilmesi ve canlı duruşu suyun ne kadar temiz olduğunu da gösteriyordu.  Akış hızı çok güçlü değil ama, bazı bölümlerde yüksekten düşen sular hızını da artırıyordu.  Kuş seslerinin ve böcek seslerinin içinde  suyun hem serinliğini hem de huzur veren sakinliği hissederek yolumuza devam ettik. Arada kenarda bir taşın üzerinde oturarak sadece suyun sesine odaklandık. Etrafımızdaki çoğu taşlar sudan nasibini almışlar.  Hepsi farklı şekillere bürünerek etrafa yayılmışlar. 

![IMG20260325141054.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQsXjHv453Cu61zC9TAxZwShrtS1giGv5GxhFhgSamfgG/IMG20260325141054.jpg)

![IMG20260325140841.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZ6KdFaXVdC4UaciGFidZzVYkrD6P1LyCgQEFuvjtFov9/IMG20260325140841.jpg)

The grasses, plants, and trees growing along the water’s edge on both sides look so colorful and vibrant that they highlight the water’s clarity and purity. As we walk through the narrow path of uneven ground and rocks along the edge, we sometimes find it difficult. Some of the stones are wet and slippery, so we need to be careful. The yellow and green grasses along the water’s edge are spread out widely. Dense stands of pine trees can be seen on the hills and mountains near the water. In the open areas left behind by the water, there are also broad-leaved trees that provide more shade. This demonstrates just how dense the vegetation around the water is. 

>Suyun kenarında sağında ve solunda yetişen otlar, bitkiler ve ağaçlar o kadar renkli ve canlı görünüyor ki; suyun tüm berraklığını ve temizliğini gözler önüne seriyor. Kenardan inişli çıkışlı oluşan dar toprağın ve taşlarının arasından yürürken zaman zaman da zorlanıyoruz. Bazı taşların yüzü ıslak ve kaygan dikkatli olmak gerekiyor. Suyun kenarındaki sarı ve yeşil otlar etraflıca dağılmışlar. Suyun yakınındaki tepelerde ve dağlarda yoğun çam ağaçları görülüyor. Suyun geride bıraktığı boş alanlarda geniş yapraklı daha gölge veren ağaçlarda var. Bu da suyun etrafındaki bitki örtüsünün ne kadar yoğun olduğunu gösteriyor. 


![IMG20260325141718.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbhev6fL3Ac8cdAjNqxrk7CnrZwD1zYtcqvxi4ddDkGfo/IMG20260325141718.jpg)

![IMG20260325140746.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbpctRj2hhg6QK1AB4LnbsEBTrVEmTHfuakV5KPLfQPk4/IMG20260325140746.jpg)

![IMG20260325142650.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaKjqgpDcmeJ2S8t3Rrj8q2DDCJchVwEXXD6SyKrvobJi/IMG20260325142650.jpg)

![IMG20260325141623.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQme3eL9KExcfLzA2xapQz9c1KyKif3nuJAch9za1LB93pL/IMG20260325141623.jpg)

I especially want to highlight the spots where the water flows with great force. In these areas, the shape and size of the rocks, along with the spaces they create, form a natural, unadorned beauty. We can see the clarity and purity of the water both on its surface and in the sparkle it leaves on the rocks and plants it strikes. Just watching the frothy spectacle created as the water flows is a great pleasure. The color of the stones varies depending on how the water strikes them. The tones and shapes of the stones, which resemble brown and black hues, also change depending on their location. 

>Suyun coşarak aktığı noktaları özellikle göstermek istiyorum. Bu alanlarda taşların şekli, büyüklüğü ve oluşturduğu boşluklar doğal sade bir güzellik oluşturmuş. Suyun berraklığını ve temizliğini hem suyun yüzünden hemde çarptıkları taşlara ve otlara bıraklığı parlaklıktan anlayabiliyoruz. Aktıkça oluşan köpüklü şölenleri izlemek bile insana büyük bir keyif veriyor. Taşların rengi suyun çarpmasına göre farklılık gösteriyor. Kahverengi ve siyah renklere benzeyen taşların tonları ve şekilleri de bulundukları yere göre değişiyor. 

![IMG20260325141712.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWccXbHXfxz5Qc2r7wz5ZFcQofUu7g2v2FRhKyHKWgXuK/IMG20260325141712.jpg)

![IMG20260325141629.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUhX9VUeozVJgFnXxhds41rtczE1Efq2cgjsoEqjFeUga/IMG20260325141629.jpg)

![IMG20260325141125.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmazR22QPTc8qWoPSbvB4Sr2wudJW9wcHQWUvDX857GbgC/IMG20260325141125.jpg)


![IMG20260325141129.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRZ94JC6EYBehuvJUdhyeDgHtMX17x6jhkuARneaQyTMo/IMG20260325141129.jpg)


![IMG20260325141100.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbw3HyWPBqjYZW9kRG28ZLrehdg4QQEovJGM4DRK7CT9C/IMG20260325141100.jpg)

We had arrived at that wide area where the waterfall flowed abundantly. Around the water, which flowed in a manner reminiscent of a long, overhanging bridge, there were mosses, aquatic plants, and rocks covered in moss. As the water flowed under the sun’s shining face, taking on a clear and clean appearance, the surrounding rocks and plants looked vibrant and colorful.  In this area, the waterfall cascades down a powerful ledge into its pools. The water arriving here flows over a natural rock formation, cascading like a fine veil to form small pools. The water, striking the rocks, flows onward in a mist of foam. It seems that natural beauties have emerged as a result of the water eroding the rock. 

>Şelalenin bol bol aktığı o geniş alana gelmiştik. Uzun taşan bir köprüyü anımsatan bir şekilde akan suyun etrafında yosun ve sucul bitkilerle beslenen otlar ve taşlar yosunlar bulunuyordu.  Güneşin parlayan yüzünde akan su berrak ve temiz bir şekle bürünürken  etrafındaki taşlar ve otlar canlı ve renkli görünüyordu.  Bu alanda şelale güçlü bir set üzerinden dökülerek havuzlarına ulaşıyor. Buraya gelen su doğal bir kayalık üzerine gelerek ince bir tül perde şeklinde akarak küçük küçük havuzlar oluşturuyor.  Kayalara çarpan sular köpükler halinde süzülerek ilerliyor. Suyun kayayı aşındırmasıyla ortaya doğal güzellikler çıkmış görünüyor.

![IMG20260325141802.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbDh9FoyHtKMbqeuX1eoRzjwgzHCHFPnQokRsbCpdqFRS/IMG20260325141802.jpg)

![IMG20260325141431.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZmQ56Ki4CtjKaZyrLkfn8UKueGrhGQAaRe9CY54H5CLe/IMG20260325141431.jpg)

After cleansing our souls with the sound of flowing water at the end of the day, we turned back to leave the waterfall.  You know how we always say that some places can only be truly understood by experiencing them firsthand? Well, Toparlar Waterfall had become just such a place for us—a place we experienced and where our souls were cleansed. 

>Günün sonunda akan suyun sesiyle ruhumuzu temizledikten sonra, şelaleden ayrılmak için geri döndük.  Hani hepimiz söyleriz ya, bazı yerler yaşanarak anlatılır. İşte toparlar şelalesi de bizim için yaşayıp, ruhumuzu temizlediğimiz bir yer olmuştu.
